articles.title: Three ways to ask a question

blocks.en: All three mean "Are you coming?". The word order of a statement changes only with inversion.
*Est-ce que* (literally "is it that") goes before any statement and turns it into a question. The word order stays. Before a vowel: *est-ce qu'il, est-ce qu'elle*.
The verb and the pronoun swap places and are joined with a hyphen.

items.note: With inversion, don't forget the hyphen.
*Est-ce que* and inversion are not combined.

items.fr: Est-ce qu'il y a un bus ?

articles.title: How to ask a question: every form

blocks.en: There are **two big families** of questions. **Yes / no questions** (*Do you like it?*) and **questions with a question word** (*Where do you live?*). Each can be formed in **three ways**: **intonation** (voice up), **est-ce que** (add before the statement), **inversion** (swap verb and subject).

**1. Intonation**: keep the statement and raise your voice (writing: add *?*). **2. Est-ce que**: put *Est-ce que* (*est-ce qu'* before a vowel) in front. **3. Inversion**: put the subject **pronoun after the verb**, joined with a hyphen. For *il, elle, on* after a vowel add **-t-**: *a-t-il, parle-t-elle*.

Put the **question word first** (informal: **last**). The word order after it is the same three ways. For a **noun subject** use *est-ce que* (*Où est-ce que Paul habite ?*) or **inversion with a pronoun** (*Où Paul habite-t-il ?*) or **simple inversion** with short verbs (*Où habite Paul ?*).

rows: Que fais-tu ? / Qu'est-ce que tu fais ?

sections.title: Qui, que, quoi: the long forms

head: person
thing
rows: Qui est-ce que tu cherches ? (Qui cherches-tu ?)

blocks.en: *Qu'est-ce que* is the question *what* + object, *qu'est-ce qui* is *what* + subject. After a **preposition** only *qui* (person) or *quoi* (thing) work: *avec qui, à quoi*.

**Compound tenses**: only the **auxiliary** is inverted (*As-tu mangé ? Est-elle partie ?*). With **two verbs** invert the first (*Peux-tu venir ?*). With **reflexive verbs** the pronoun stays in front (*Te lèves-tu ?*, *T'es-tu levé ?*). **Pronouns** stay in front of the verb (*Le vois-tu ? L'as-tu vu ?*). **Negative** questions put *ne ... pas* around the inverted block (*N'as-tu pas faim ?*).

items.fr: Le professeur a-t-il corrigé les tests ?
items.en: Did the teacher mark the tests?
Why did you get up so early?

blocks.en: **N'est-ce pas ?** at the end asks for agreement (*Il fait beau, n'est-ce pas ?*). In speech also **non ?**, **hein ?**, **d'accord ?** Answer with **oui / non**; to contradict a **negative question** use **si**.

items.en: You're not coming? – Yes, I am!

a: Est-ce que tu aimes le chocolat ?

articles.title: Answering: oui, non, si, moi aussi, pas du tout

blocks.en: A short answer needs only **oui** (yes), **non** (no) or **si** (yes, to a **negative** question). You can add a short phrase to be polite or precise. Use **moi aussi / moi non plus** to agree, **pas moi / moi si** to disagree.
**Si** is the **yes that contradicts a negative**. **Oui** answers a positive question. If you agree with a negative question you say **non**.

items.en: Aren't you hungry? Yes, I am.
items.wrong: Tu n'as pas faim ? – Oui, j'ai faim.
items.fr: Tu n'as pas faim ? – [[Si]], j'ai faim.

items.en: Aren't you coming? No, I'm not.
items.wrong: Tu ne viens pas ? – Si, je ne viens pas.
items.fr: Tu ne viens pas ? – [[Non]], je ne viens pas.

blocks.en: To answer a question fully, **repeat the verb** instead of the pronoun: *Tu viens ? – Oui, je viens.* Do not say *Oui, je fais* instead of the verb in the question. Short answers like *Je le crois* or *Je l'espère* replace a clause (see the neutral *le*).

items.fr: Tu parles français ? – Oui, je le parle un peu.
items.en: Do you speak French? – Yes, a little.

items.fr: Il vient demain ? – Je pense que oui.
items.en: Is he coming tomorrow? – I think so.

items.fr: Tu as des frères ? – Non, je n'en ai pas.
items.en: Do you have brothers? – No, I don't.

items.fr: Tu aimes les araignées ? – Pas du tout.
items.en: Do you like spiders? – Not at all.

items.fr: Tu n'es pas content ? – Si, très.

articles.title: Question words and where they go

blocks.en: The same question can be asked in three ways. The question word is either **at the end** (speech), or **at the start** with *est-ce que* or with inversion.
*Que* stands at the start (*Qu'est-ce que tu fais ?*), *quoi* at the end or after a preposition (*Tu fais quoi ? À quoi tu penses ?*). The answer to *pourquoi* is *parce que*.

items.en: How many brothers do you have?

checks.en: Where do you live? In Prague.

checks.fr: ___ est-ce que tu ne viens pas ? Parce que je suis malade.
checks.en: Why aren't you coming? Because I'm ill.

checks.task_en: Put the question word at the start (with est-ce que)

blocks.en: *Quel* means "which, what", stands **before a noun** and agrees with it. All four forms sound the same.
*Quel* can also stand before *être* and then agrees with the noun after it: *Quelle est ta couleur préférée ?* (What is your favourite colour?)

blocks.title: Exclamations
blocks.en: *Quel* is also used in exclamations: *Quel beau temps !* (What lovely weather!) *Quelle chance !* (What luck!)

items.en: Which film do you want to see?

items.fr: À quelle heure tu te lèves ?
items.en: What time do you get up?

blocks.en: With inversion the **pronoun and the verb** swap places and are joined with a hyphen: *tu as → as-tu ?* It is the careful style. It is rare in speech but common in texts and at school.
When the verb ends in a vowel and the pronoun starts with a vowel (*il, elle, on*), a *-t-* is inserted between them so it can be pronounced: *A-t-il faim ? Va-t-elle venir ?*

sections.title: With a noun and in compound tenses

blocks.en: When the subject is a noun, it stays at the start and a pronoun is added after the verb: *Paul vient-il ?* (Is Paul coming?)
In compound tenses the pronoun swaps with the **auxiliary**: *As-tu mangé ? Es-tu allé au cinéma ?*

blocks.en: The interrogative *qui* is always about a **person**, *que / quoi* about a **thing**. (With relative pronouns it is different.)

When you ask about a thing that is the **subject** (what is happening, what interests you), use *qu'est-ce qui*: *Qu'est-ce qui se passe ?* (What is happening?) *Qu'est-ce qui t'intéresse ?* (What interests you?)

items.note: After *qui* comes the verb straight away (the thing is the subject). After *que* come subject and verb.

checks.en: What are you doing this weekend?
Who are you going to the cinema with?
a: Avec qui tu vas au cinéma ?
Avec qui est-ce que tu vas au cinéma ?
Tu vas au cinéma avec qui ?

articles.title: Preposition + question word: à qui, avec quoi, depuis quand

blocks.en: In French the **preposition always goes before the question word** (never at the end as in English). For people use **preposition + qui**, for things **preposition + quoi**, and for time, place and quantity the question words *quand, où, combien, quel*.

head: question
meaning
answer
rows: Who are you going out with?
At whose place do you sleep?

head: question
meaning
rows: Since when have you lived here?
Depuis combien de temps apprends-tu le français ?
For how long have you been learning French?
À quelle heure commence le film ?
At what time does the film start?
In which town do you live?

blocks.en: *Depuis quand* and *depuis combien de temps* are followed by the **present**: *Depuis quand habites-tu ici ?* (not the passé composé).

In speech the question word can stay at the end of the sentence with the preposition in front of it: **Tu parles à qui ? Tu penses à quoi ? Tu habites depuis quand ?** The preposition **still comes before** *qui* or *quoi*.

items.fr: Avec qui est-ce que tu vas au cinéma ?
items.en: Who are you going to the cinema with?
Since when have you been ill?
What time do you get up?

De quoi est-ce que nous parlons ?

checks.en: Since when have you lived here?

blocks.en: *Lequel* means "which one (of them)". It **replaces** *quel* + the noun that has already been mentioned.

items.en: I have two T-shirts. Which one do you want?

blocks.en: With the prepositions *à* and *de* it merges like an article: *auquel, auxquels, auxquelles* and *duquel, desquels, desquelles*. The form with *la* stays: *à laquelle, de laquelle*.

items.en: Which of these dresses do you prefer?

items.fr: Il y a deux bus. Lequel va au centre ?
items.en: There are two buses. Which one goes to the centre?

items.fr: Tu penses à un jeu ? Auquel ?
items.en: Are you thinking of a game? Which one?

blocks.en: An indirect question is a question hidden inside a sentence: "I don't know **where he lives**." It has **normal word order** (subject + verb), no *est-ce que*, no inversion and no question mark.

items.en: Where does he live? → I don't know where he lives.
items.fr: Où habite-t-il ? → Je ne sais pas [[où il habite]].

blocks.en: A yes / no question → *si* (whether). *Qu'est-ce que* → *ce que*, *qu'est-ce qui* → *ce qui*. The other question words stay.

items.en: I don't know what he wants.

items.fr: Je ne comprends pas ce que tu dis.
